newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia wheat may be at bottom - Dresdner/NFF.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia wheat may be at bottom - Dresdner/NFF.

text.p: Prices for wheat in Australian dollar terms may have bottomed during November, according to the international commodity price review released by the National Farmers' Federation (NFF) and Dresdner Australia International.

NFF's director of economic policy, Todd Ritchie, said wheat prices were likely to remain under pressure in the short term, with Australian exports facing tough competition, especially from Argentina, which also had a bumper crop this year.

"Prices weakened earlier this month with the Australian Wheat Board pool price estimate for Australian Standard White revised downward by A$15 per tonne to A$175 per tonne in the first week of November," Ritchie said in a statement.

But the revision of U.S. and global ending stock downward was the first positive news for growers for some time from the U.S. Department of Agriculture, leading to a five percent jump in the market price to A$210 per tonne on November 14, Ritchie said.
The wool market was suppressed by heavy spring offerings and beef prices fell slightly during the month, he said.
"Overall the special drawing rights (SDR) commodity price index fell by 1.0 percent in November, but rose in A$ terms by 0.3 per cent, due to a slightly weaker Australian dollar," he said.
Dresdner chief economist Rob Henderson said non-rural SDR prices fell by 0.4 percent in November, although they were 5.3 percent higher than the same time last year.
"In A$ terms, prices increased by 0.9 per cent, with metal prices improving by 1.2 percent," Henderson said in a statement.

"The A$ pushed above U.S. 80 cents on November 20, reflecting on-going international demand for Australian fixed interest securities and a base metals inspired rally in commodity futures terms," he said.
The move was consistent with Dresdner's view that firming growth by the G-7 countries would push the currency higher in 1997, he said.
